Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avemæ, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. ATTY. PETER ELFRED A. LASMARIAS City Legal Officer City of Tangub Dear Atty. Lasmarias: This has reference your letter dated 27 February 2019 requesting for the Department's opinion on whether or not the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) may prescribe, and compel thereof, the manner of selection and appointment of local college officials, teaching and non-teaching personnel. You submitted the queries quoted in verbatim as follows: I. Whether or not the Commission on Higher Education or CHED has the legal authority to prescribe, as well as compel observance thereof, the manner of selection and appointment of the President, Vice-President, Deans, Directors, Registrar, Administrative Officer, Accountant, Teaching and Non- teaching personnel of a Local College considering that Section 8(m) of Republic Act No. 7722 or the Higher Education Act of 1994 merely limited CHED's power to review the charters of institutions of higher learning and recommend appropriate measures; 2. Whether or not CHED Memorandum Order (CMO) No. 32, Series of 2006, CMO No. 04, Series of 2007 and CMO No. 42, Series of 2016 which prescribe the manner of selection and appointment of President, Deans, Directors, Registrar, Administrative Officer, Accountant, teaching and non-teaching personnel of a Local College contravene the express provisions of the Section 76 of Republic Act 7160 or the Local Government Code of the Philippines which allows the Local Government to design and implement its own organizational structure and staffing pattern and Section 455.b.I.v. thereof which grants the power to the City Mayor to appoint all officials and employees whose salaries and wages are wholly or mainly paid out of city funds and whose appointments are not otherwise provided for in this Code, as well as those he may be authorized by law to appoint; and 3. Whether or not the Local Government of Tangub City should insist in its authority to prescribe and implement its own S. 202

staffing pattern with respect to the administrative personnel of GADTC and the Local Chief Executive's power to appoint them, particularly the College President, under the Local Government Code. The above quoted queries are interrelated. Separate discussions in attempt to answer each question will be redundant. Thus, we will provide a consolidated answer to the same. Our view is that CHED has authority to prescribe the manner and selection of appointment of officials and manpower as stated in its Memorandum Order No. 32, series of 2006, Memorandum Order No. 4, series of 2007, and Memorandum Order No. 42, series of 2016. We herein make reference to Republic Act No. 7722, otherwise known as the Higher Education Act of 1994 as its legal basis. In Section 8(h) and (m), it states: "Section 8. Powers and Functions of the Commission. -The Commission shall have the following powers and functions: xxx h. rationalize programs and institutions Of higher learning and set standards, policies and guidelines for the creation of new ones as well as the conversion or elevation of schools to institutions of higher learning, subject to budgetary limitations and the number of institutions of higher learning in the province or region where creation, conversion or elevation is sought to be made; xxx m. review the charters of institutions of higher learning and state universities and colleges including the chairmanship and membership of their governing bodies and recommend appropriate measures as basis for necessary action; xxx" It is our view that the phrase "rationalize programs and institutions" refers to the duty and power of the CHED to standardize all institutions of higher learning in the whole country. Accordingly, the word "institution" is another term for "organization," which refers to the people that comprise it. Thus, to our mind, prescribing the minimum requirements as to the membership of the governing bodies and the organizational composition of the local colleges and universities and their manner of selection by CHED has legal basis. Further, such exercise of authority protects and promotes the right of the students to quality education. The right to quality education of the students is not a priority concern limited within the responsibility and governance of the local governments but best remains to be shared with national government. This is to standardize and even out the playing field as to the access of all the students in the country to quality education. It is no less than the Constitution that places a great value on education that it mandates the State to give priority to education, science and technology,

arts, culture, and sports to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development,l and to recognize the vital role of the youth in nation building and to promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being.2 Moreover, the Supreme Court held: While the Constitution indeed mandates the State to provide quality education, the determination of what constitutes quality education is best left with the political departments who have the necessary knowledge, expertise, and resources to determine the same. The deliberations of the Constitutional Commission again are very instructive: Now, Madam President, we have added the word "quality" before "education" to send appropriate signals to the government that, in the exercise of its supervisory and regulatory powers, it should first set satisfactory minimum requirements in all areas: curriculum, faculty, internal administration, library, laboratory class and other facilities, et cetera, and it should see to it that satisfactory minimum requirements are met by all educational institutions, both public and private. When we speak of quality education we have in mind such matters, among others, as curriculum development, development of learning resources and instructional materials, upgrading of library and laboratory facilities, innovations in educational technology and teaching methodologies, improvement of research quality, and others. Here and in many other provisions on education, the principal focus of attention and concern is the students. I would like to say that in my view there is a slogan when we speak of quality of education that I fee/ we should be aware of, which is, "Better than ever is not enough." In other words, even if the quality of education is good now, we should attempt to keep on improving it.219 (Emphasis supplied) 3 Further, our view is that the exercise of CHED of the authority to prescribe such rules and regulations does not intend to undermine the authority granted to the concerned local governments, under Sections 7 and 455(b)(I)(v) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, to organize its structure and staffing pattern. Sections 76 and 455(b)(1)(v) of RA 7160 are general provisions granting the Local Government Units the power to determine its human resource requirements in order to maintain a local government 1 Section 17, Article II of the 1987 Constitution 2 Section 13, Article II of the 1987 Constitution 3 G.R. NO. 216930, October 09, 2018, G.R. NO. 217451, October 9, 2018, G.R. NO. 217752, October 9, 2018, G.R. NO. 218045, October 9, 2018, G.R. NO. 218098, October 9, 2018, G.R. NO. 218123, October 9, 2018, G.R. NO. 218465, October 9, 2018

responsive to the needs of its constituency and an uninterrupted provision of services for the general welfare of its people. Notwithstanding, the aforecited provisions of RA 7722 are specific provisions catered for the institutions of higher learning with the objective to protect and promote the quality education. Further, the Local Chief Executive is the Chairman of the Governing Board, which is the highest policy-making body of the LUCs and the appointing body for the President and the one that confirms the appointments by the President. Accordingly, if the GADTC is an institution for higher learning or is applying for an elevation as such, then the rules on the appointment of its President and administrative personnel shall be governed by pertinent CHED issuances, which dictate that its President shall be appointed by the governing board upon the recommendation of the search committee and that the President of the college shall appoint the Vice-President(s), Dean(s), Directors, Registrar, Administrative Officer, Accountants, faculty, non-teaching personnel and other officials subject to the confirmation of the governing board. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 ndersecretary LLLS/42T
